name: Lymphatic Ferrostatic Occlusion Rifle
description:
The LFOR-3 delivers a payload of magnetically responsive ferrofluid nanoparticles via a pressurized aerosol bolt that disperses on skin contact and penetrates subcutaneously through follicular and sweat gland channels. Once embedded in the subcutaneous tissue, an external magnetic pulse from the rifle's secondary emitter aligns and compacts the particles within lymphatic capillaries, causing immediate mechanical occlusion. The resulting blockage triggers rapid localized lymphedema — extreme fluid accumulation in the affected limb or region.

The swelling is not merely cosmetic. Within minutes, the pressure in occluded tissue exceeds compartment syndrome thresholds, causing excruciating pain, loss of motor function, and if untreated, tissue necrosis. The weapon can be tuned to affect a single limb or, with a wider dispersal bolt, to seed multiple lymphatic regions simultaneously. Unlike many exotic weapons in its class, the LFOR-3 is deliberately designed for survivability — the manufacturer positions it as a 'non-lethal incapacitation system' — though death from secondary infection or untreated compartment syndrome is common in populations without access to quality medical care.

Helix Biosystems developed the ferrostatic occlusion mechanism from research into targeted lymphatic drug delivery. The weaponized application was funded through a subsidiary with deliberately obscured corporate parentage. The rifle is now quietly distributed to private security firms as a 'humane deterrent,' with Helix maintaining that adverse outcomes are the result of inadequate post-exposure medical response rather than the weapon itself.
specifications:
effective range: 5–35 meters
bolt type: Pressurized aerosol dispersal, contact-detonated
particle payload: 0.4 mL ferrofluid suspension per bolt
magnetic pulse range: Up to 20 meters post-dispersal
magazine capacity: 12 bolts
onset time: Swelling visible within 90 seconds, incapacitation within 4–7 minutes
weight: 2.6 kg loaded
reversal: Magnetic dispersal wand (sold separately, Helix Biosystems)
tactical_use: Corporate security teams deploy the LFOR-3 for crowd incapacitation at entry control points, targeting the legs to drop subjects without lethal force. In coercive interrogation contexts, operators target the hands and face to maximize distress. The magnetic dispersal wand — which reverses the occlusion — is used as a bargaining tool during detentions. Skilled operators can target specific limbs with the narrow-cone bolt to selectively incapacitate without affecting mobility entirely.
cultural_context: Stonewood has become notorious in GLMZ's poorer districts, where private security firms use it liberally at corporate-owned transit hubs and housing estates. The term 'got stoned' refers to being shot by the LFOR-3, and the distinctive puffy, hard-skinned appearance of untreated lymphedema victims — those who couldn't afford or access the dispersal wand — is visible enough on the streets that it has become a marker of class victimhood. Helix Biosystems' ongoing PR positioning of the weapon as 'humane' is a source of bitter public satire.
known_users: Mira Osei, a bounty hunter who prefers live captures
story_hooks: A district health worker is documenting an epidemic of untreated lymphedema cases in a corporate housing estate �� she needs help getting the evidence out before Helix Biosystems' lawyers bury it.
A stolen shipment of dispersal wands is being held ransom by a gang who understand exactly what leverage they have over people who've been shot with Stonewood.
A player character is hit with the LFOR-3 during a routine job gone wrong and has hours to find a dispersal wand before permanent tissue damage sets in.
Helix Biosystems is quietly developing a version with a delayed magnetic trigger — meaning victims can be shot and not know it until they're far from the scene.

physical_description.visual_profile: A sleek, medical-aesthetic rifle with organic curves that obscure its true purpose. The design evokes laboratory equipment more than a weapon — angular yet flowing, with a tapered barrel and integrated magnetic emitter housing. The overall impression is clinical precision wrapped in corporate restraint.
physical_description.dimensions: 118 cm length overall, 42 cm height including magnetic coil array, 8 cm barrel diameter. Magazine well sits forward of the trigger guard.
physical_description.weight_description: Hefty but well-balanced — 2.6 kg loaded feels substantial without being unwieldy. The weight distribution favors the forward section, making sustained aim require consistent upper body tension.
physical_description.primary_material: Aerospace-grade polymer composite frame with embedded conductive alloy lattice for magnetic coil integration. Barrel section is reinforced titanium-carbon weave.
physical_description.finish: Matte charcoal with brushed chrome accents on the magnetic emitter ring and magazine release. The polymer shows a subtle iridescent sheen under direct light — an intentional design choice suggesting biopharma sophistication rather than military hardware.
physical_description.color_scheme: Charcoal grey primary with chrome and teal accent lines running along the magnetic array housing. A small helix motif in teal appears on the receiver — Helix Biosystems branding.
physical_description.grip_texture: Rubberized polymer with subtle micro-texturing designed for gloved operation. Ergonomic, almost surgical in its attention to hand geometry.
distinctive_features: Integrated magnetic emitter ring surrounding the barrel junction — copper-colored coil visible through translucent polymer section
Secondary targeting readout on the stock — small LED display showing dispersal cone angle and magnetic pulse calibration
Pressurized bolt chamber visible through reinforced viewport on the magazine well
Faint warning labels in corp-standard sans-serif along the barrel: λ BIOHAZARD PAYLOAD, FERROSTATIC CLASS III
Charging handle is recessed and requires deliberate engagement — suggests operator care and precision over rapid deployment
Heat dissipation vents along the magnetic housing emit faint blue glow when system is armed
physical_description.manufacturer_markings: HELIX BIOSYSTEMS stamped in minimal serif font on the receiver above the magazine well. Serial number on the stock in small white text. A small regulatory stamp in the lower receiver states 'NON-LETHAL INCAPACITATION SYSTEM — MEDICAL RESPONSE RECOMMENDED.'
physical_description.condition_typical: Well-maintained to pristine in corporate security contexts. Field-used examples show minor polymer scratches and occasional ferrofluid residue stains around the magazine well. Black market variants exhibit jury-rigged replacements for magnetic coils and mismatched ammunition.
